events.text: A crowded roadside inn, and only one seat free: across from a plain-looking traveller eating noodles. The innkeeper, white as rice, whispers the name as she pours your tea. It is {npc}, {npc_title}. {He} looks up, and waits to see what you will do with that.

choices.text: Pour {him} wine and ask about the martial path

mem.note: poured my wine and listened like a student

ok.log: {He} talks until the lamps are lit. Half of it is about noodles. The other half you will think about for ten years.

fail.log: {He} answers in single words and leaves early. Still: you ate noodles with {npc}.

choices.text: "Teach me one thing, master." Bow to the floor

mem.note: bowed in a crowded inn and meant it

ok.log: {He} shows you how to hold a chopstick so that it is a sword. You never hold a sword the same way again.

fail.log: The whole inn watches you bow. {He} finishes {his} noodles, pays for yours, and leaves. It is either a kindness or a lesson.

choices.text: Eat your noodles. Masters like to be left alone

effects.log: You eat in companionable silence. As {he} goes, {he} taps your table twice. The innkeeper says that means {he} will remember you.

events.text: A letter in a hand like a sword cut: {npc}, {npc_title}, is holding a banquet for the masters of three provinces, and there is a seat with your name on it. At the bottom: "Bring your appetite. The noodles are better here."

choices.text: Go, and hold your own among the great

mem.note: held their own at my table

ok.log: You talk with masters whose names you grew up on. By the end, three of them know yours.

fail.log: You are the youngest and least important person there, and everybody knows it. You learn a great deal by keeping quiet.

choices.text: Go, and challenge the loudest master there to a friendly bout

ok.log: You win. {npc} laughs so hard {he} spills {his} wine. That bout is talked about for years.

fail.log: You lose, well. {npc} toasts you anyway: "To someone who will win next time."

events.text: A messenger in white at your gate: {npc}, {npc_title}, has heard of you, and invites you to a sparring match on the peak of a mountain at dawn. No crowd. No stakes. Only two people who want to know.

choices.text: Climb the mountain and fight with everything

mem.note: beat me on the peak at dawn

ok.log: At sunrise you land the last blow, by a hair. {npc} sits down in the snow and laughs. "Well. Now I have to train again."

mem.note: fought me honestly on the peak

fail.log: You lose, the way water loses to a mountain. {npc} helps you up and shows you the three moves that did it.

choices.text: Go, but ask to watch {him} practise instead

effects.log: An hour of {npc} moving through forms in the dawn light. It is the most beautiful thing you have ever seen, and you understand about a third of it.

events.text: {npc}, {npc_title}, comes to your sect in person, which has never happened before, and asks to see your disciples train. Afterwards {he} asks, very politely, if {he} may take your most gifted one away to study under {him} for three years.

choices.text: Agree. A student should have the best teacher

mem.note: gave me their best disciple to teach

effects.log: Your disciple goes down the mountain with {npc}, terrified and shining. Three years later {he} sends your disciple back a realm higher, with a letter that says only: "Good teacher."

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach here, for a season, all of them

mem.note: out-bargained me for a season of teaching

ok.log: {npc} stays a whole spring. Every disciple in your hall trains under one of the greatest masters alive. You train too, at the back, and nobody mentions it.

fail.log: "One student is a gift," {npc} says. "A whole hall is a job." {He} leaves, a little cooler.

choices.text: Refuse. Your disciples are yours to teach

effects.log: {npc} bows, approving. "Good. A master who gives students away too easily does not deserve them."

events.text: {npc}, {npc_title}, has not forgotten the dawn you beat {him} on the mountain. The jianghu says {he} has been training for nothing else since. Now {he} is at your gate, and this time there is a crowd.

choices.text: Fight {him} again, in front of everyone

ok.log: Twice. {npc} kneels in the dust and then, unexpectedly, laughs. "Again in five years," {he} says. You suspect you have a friend for life.

fail.deathCause: a ranked master who came back for a rematch
fail.log: {npc} wins. {He} does not gloat. {He} bows the exact bow you gave {him} that dawn, and leaves the score even.

choices.text: Refuse the crowd. Offer a rematch on the same peak, at dawn, alone

effects.log: {npc} stares, then grins. "Yes. That is right." The rematch on the peak is the best fight of your life, and nobody ever learns who won.
